justification: Contributes Context-ReAct's five context operations (Skip/Compress/Rollback/Snippet/Delete) reshaping the working trajectory; a lab-only agent measured on BrowseComp and three other search benchmarks.
ContextCurator is an RL-trained policy that prunes working-memory noise while preserving reasoning anchors; evidence is WebArena and DeepSearch success/token numbers, a lab prototype not in use.
ContextWeaver builds a dependency graph of prior steps and selects context for future actions, i.e. what carries across steps; validated on SWE-Bench Verified and Lite pass@1, lab only.
Headline is a diagnostic study naming premature termination and comparing seven context-management methods as an instrument for loop failure, run over three benchmarks and four models in the lab.
Audits one named mechanism, context compaction, showing it drops governance constraints, and pins them; evidence is 1,323 episodes with policy-in-context versus post-compaction conditions compared.
PRO-LONG is a context-management harness deciding what is saved from the environment and loaded back via programmatic memory; measured on the ARC-AGI-3 public game set against other harnesses.

IDSS keeps an explicit situation state of grounded facts and constraints outside the dialogue history, the paper's stated alternative to history-centric context management; tested on three interactive benchmarks.
TopoPrior learns reusable priors over agent collaboration topologies, i.e. the arrangement itself, replacing per-query topology search; evaluated on multi-domain reasoning benchmarks in the lab.
A puppeteer orchestrator dynamically sequences and prioritises which agent acts next, a claim about the collaboration structure; supported by closed- and open-domain benchmark runs, no deployment.
OrchRM scores orchestration quality from intermediate multi-agent artifacts to guide orchestrator training and MAS scaling; lab evidence across math, web QA and multi-hop reasoning benchmarks.
Empirical audit of the multi-turn propose-and-vote orchestration protocol, including whether authorship and running votes are visible; benchmarked on GPQA-Diamond, IFEval and MuSR in the lab.
MACA learns a structural prior over which agents participate and interact, then a policy orchestrating them, a contribution about coordination structure; benchmark accuracy and token gains only.

GUARDIAN's contribution is the detection judgement: a temporal-graph anomaly detector that flags hallucinated or erroneous nodes and edges before they propagate; accuracy reported against baselines in lab experiments.
LEMON generates an executable orchestration specification of roles, capacities and dependency structure, the arrangement itself; validated on six reasoning and coding benchmarks, not in practice.
The artefact is an instrument, a mean-field entropy dynamics model plus the IWG pipeline synthesising checkpoint-dense benchmarks, used to diagnose orchestrator collapse; fitted to lab trajectories.
HASSUM's novelty is the semantic entropy/density confidence signal that gates outputs, triggering verification, reprompting or reselection; evaluated on StrategyQA, JailbreakBench and TruthfulQA.
AdaptOrch routes task DAGs to one of four orchestration topologies, claiming topology choice dominates model choice; validated on SWE-bench, GPQA and RAG tasks in the lab, no field use.
Headline artefact is a scalable benchmark plus reference scaffold and evaluation protocol for deliberative collaboration, used to systematically evaluate representative LLMs in the lab.

MPDF replaces fixed collaboration protocols with a learned decentralised policy over Persist/Refine/Concede, i.e. what agents do to each other in deliberation; gains shown on five reasoning benchmarks.
LAMaS learns the multi-agent execution graph with critical-path credit assignment and prunes agent interactions at runtime, a claim about the arrangement; four lab benchmarks, latency and accuracy.
DAAO generates query-specific multi-agent workflows, allocating operators and routing across heterogeneous LLMs by predicted difficulty; evidence is accuracy and efficiency on six benchmarks.
MARS prescribes an author/reviewer/meta-reviewer role structure that avoids reviewer-to-reviewer traffic, a claim about the arrangement; compared with MAD and other strategies on multiple benchmarks.
INFRAMIND conditions topology, role selection and per-step model routing on live serving-infrastructure state; evaluated across five benchmarks on a lab cluster, not a production deployment study.
A structural causal action model scores and reweights candidate actions, deciding what the agent does next; validated on Overcooked-AI across five tasks and four LLMs in AI-AI and human-AI settings.
Tests how orchestration structure itself, visible leader versus invisible orchestrator versus flat, changes agent behaviour, via a preregistered 3x2 experiment of 365 lab runs on Claude Sonnet 4.5.
